s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive periorbital swelling with erythema and destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus
salient_findings: Progressive right periorbital swelling of three weeks’ duration
Destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus
Rapid enlargement of the mass on serial imaging
key_facts: 27-month-old girl
Progressive right periorbital swelling of three weeks’ duration
No preceding trauma
Initial treatment with ophthalmic ointment and eye drops without improvement
Diagnosed with periorbital cellulitis and treated with oral cefaclor for two weeks without improvement
C-reactive protein level of 0.59 mg/dL
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 57 mm/h
Orbital CT scan showed a destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus
MRI showed heterogeneous enhancement after contrast administration and invasion of the ipsilateral inferior orbital wall and extraconal space
Serial imaging over two weeks showed rapid enlargement of the mass

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly enlarging mass with destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and invasion of surrounding tissues

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and periorbital swelling with erythema

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone tumor that can cause rapid enlargement of a mass and invasion of surrounding tissues

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and periorbital swelling with erythema, with potential for rapid growth

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly enlarging mass with destructive lesion in the maxillary sinus and potential for systemic involvement

raw.rationale: The rapid enlargement of the mass, destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the right maxillary sinus, and heterogeneous enhancement after contrast administration are consistent with a highly aggressive tumor such as Rhabdomyosarcoma, which is a common soft tissue sarcoma in children.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: More commonly affects the long bones and pelvis, and the imaging findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with nasal obstruction and epistaxis, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Would not typically cause a destructive lesion centered on the anterior wall of the maxillary sinus
